Right here! Everything cost thirty-eight euros, so here is twelve in change.

Wait a second, Clara... which packet of butter did you buy?
The one in gold paper from the top shelf. Why?
That is sea-salt butter! My sweet rolls take unsalted butter!

Can we serve salted butter with sweet strawberry jam?

meanings.note: Las nueve = nine o'clock.

examples.text: El tren llega a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The train arrives at nine on the dot.
We saw a nine out of ten.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Café con leche = white coffee.

examples.text: La leche es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The milk is very important here.
We talk about the milk.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Huevos revueltos = scrambled eggs.

examples.trans: The egg is here.

examples.text: Vemos los huevos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eggs from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Means both 'apple' and a square block of city buildings.

examples.trans: The apple is here.

examples.text: Vemos las manzanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the apples from the door.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Feminine: la campeona; plural: los campeones.

examples.trans: The champion is here.

examples.text: Vemos los campeones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the champions from the door.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.
The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Machine or pot for brewing coffee.

examples.trans: The coffee maker is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cafeteras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coffee makers from the door.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Con rapidez = quickly.

examples.text: La rapidez es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The speed is very important here.
We talk about the speed.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Recibimos a los huéspedes con té.
examples.trans: We welcome guests with tea.

examples.text: Esta mañana recibí una carta certificada.
examples.trans: This morning I received a registered letter.

meanings.note: Owner of a small neighbourhood shop (tienda).

examples.trans: The shopkeeper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tenderos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shopkeepers from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.trans: We have the same job.
I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuesta).

examples.trans: Breakfast costs six euros.

examples.text: Todo el pedido costó treinta euros.
examples.trans: The whole order cost thirty euros.

meanings.note: Treinta y cinco = thirty-five.

examples.text: Nos dan treinta días de plazo.
examples.trans: They give us thirty days' notice.

examples.text: Son las nueve y treinta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is nine thirty-five.

meanings.note: Las ocho = eight o'clock.

examples.text: Abrimos la puerta a las ocho.
examples.trans: We open the door at eight.
The guesthouse has eight rooms.

meanings.note: Currency of Spain.

examples.text: Un café con leche y dos churros calientes cuestan apenas tres euros.
examples.trans: A coffee with milk and two hot churros cost barely three euros.

meanings.note: Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.
It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Las doce = twelve o'clock.

examples.text: El reloj da las doce al mediodía.
examples.trans: The clock strikes twelve at noon.

examples.text: Aquí tienes doce euros de cambio.
examples.trans: Here is twelve euros in change.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

cambiar.gloss: to change; to swap; to exchange

meanings.en: to change; to swap; to exchange
meanings.note: Cambiar de habitación/camisa uses de before the noun.

examples.trans: I change the towels every morning.
We moved the table to a new spot.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.
Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Las once = eleven o'clock.

examples.text: Son las once y veinte de la mañana.
examples.trans: It is eleven twenty in the morning.
Eleven clean chairs remain.

meanings.note: Used alone as an enthusiastic 'Exactly!'.

examples.trans: It is an exact piece.

examples.text: ¡Exacto! Ya eres una más del equipo.
examples.trans: Exactly! You are already one of the team.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on ú.

examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Diez, once, doce. Exacto hasta la última moneda. ¡Gracias!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last coin. Thank you!

meanings.note: Metal coin.

examples.trans: The coin is here.

examples.text: Vemos las monedas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coins from the door.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Wrapped package or parcel.

examples.trans: The parcel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los paquetes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the parcels from the door.

meanings.note: Spread on warm morning toast.

examples.text: La mantequilla es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The butter is very important here.
We talk about the butter.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Compro pan caliente en la esquina.
examples.trans: I buy warm bread on the corner.
Yesterday we bought six yellow lemons.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.trans: The paper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los papeles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the papers from the door.

meanings.note: Describes gold colour or golden-brown baked crust.

examples.trans: It is a golden piece.

examples.text: El del papel dorado del estante de arriba. ¿Por qué?
examples.trans: The one in gold paper from the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Wooden wall or cupboard shelf.

examples.trans: The shelf is here.

examples.text: Vemos los estantes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shelves from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Con sal = salted; sin sal = unsalted.

examples.text: La sal es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The salt is very important here.
We talk about the salt.

meanings.note: In azul marino, invariable or agreeing depending on style.

examples.trans: It is a marine piece.

examples.text: ¿Esa es la vieja maleta azul marino del taller del abuelo?
examples.trans: Is that the old dark-blue bag from Grandfather's workshop?

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Breakfast pastry or soft bread roll.

examples.trans: The sweet roll is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bollos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sweet rolls from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; los dulces = sweets/pastries.

examples.trans: It is a sweet piece.

examples.text: ¿Podemos servir mantequilla salada con mermelada dulce de fresa?
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with sweet strawberry jam?

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.
He left home without a coat.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

examples.trans: Oh, I nearly forgot my umbrella!
Goodness, what a fright you gave me!

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Tener prisa = be in a rush; ¡Date prisa! = Hurry up!

examples.trans: The hurry is here.

examples.text: Vemos las prisas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hurrys from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg parezco.

examples.text: Este rincón parece un jardín secreto.
examples.trans: This corner looks like a secret garden.
The idea seemed excellent to us.

meanings.note: Igual que = just like / the same as.

examples.trans: It is a same piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sirvo, sirve, sirvió).

examples.text: Servimos desayuno caliente de ocho a diez.
examples.trans: We serve hot breakfast from eight to ten.

examples.text: La encargada sirvió tres tazas de té de menta.
examples.trans: La encargada served three cups of mint tea.

meanings.note: Opposite of dulce.

examples.trans: It is a salty piece.

examples.text: ¿Podemos servir mantequilla salada con mermelada dulce de fresa?
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with sweet strawberry jam?

meanings.note: Fruit preserve eaten at breakfast.

examples.trans: The jam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mermeladas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the jams from the door.

meanings.note: Mermelada de fresa = strawberry jam.

examples.trans: The strawberry is here.

examples.text: Vemos las fresas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the strawberries from the door.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Colloquial favourite in Spain: va fatal = it is running terribly.

examples.trans: It is a terrible piece.

examples.text: Un momento: ¡con mermelada va fatal, pero en los huevos revueltos queda riquísima!
examples.trans: Hold on: with jam it is terrible, yet in scrambled eggs it tastes delicious!

meanings.note: Core contrast conjunction.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera, pero dentro se está bien.
examples.trans: It is cold outside, yet inside it is cosy.

examples.text: Es pequeño, pero tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: It is small, but it has lots of light.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Huevos revueltos = scrambled eggs.

examples.trans: It is a scrambled piece.

examples.text: Los huevos revueltos están deliciosos, Clara. ¡Felicite a Rocío de mi parte!
examples.trans: The scrambled eggs are delicious, Clara. Tell Rocio my compliments!

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

meanings.note: Absolute superlative of rico (c -> qu before í).

examples.trans: It is a delicious piece.
delicious

meanings.note: Por lo menos = at least; echar de menos = to miss; a menos que = unless.

examples.trans: It is ten to eight.

examples.text: Por lo menos ya no llueve.
examples.trans: At least it is no longer raining.

meanings.note: Nada mal = not bad at all; menos mal = thank goodness.

examples.text: Nada mal para el primer día.
examples.trans: Not bad at all for the first day.
Thank goodness you brought an umbrella!

pensar.gloss: to think; to plan to (pensar + infinitive)

meanings.en: to think; to plan to (pensar + infinitive)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: pienso).

examples.text: Pienso abrir la cafetería a las ocho.
examples.trans: I plan to open the cafe at eight.
What do you think of this blue paint?

meanings.note: Used both as adjective and adverb (corre rápido).

examples.trans: It is a fast piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Un paraguas a tiempo salva el paseo.
examples.trans: A timely umbrella saves the walk.

examples.text: Tu idea rápida salvó todo el desayuno.
examples.trans: Your quick idea saved the whole breakfast.

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.trans: The breakfast is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desayunos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the breakfasts from the door.

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!
The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!
